chunks: Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated from Safwan, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about three people who entered into Tawaf. He said: Each one of them said to his companion, 'Guard/remember the Tawaf.' When they thought they had finished, one said, 'I have seven shawt (stages),' the other said, 'I have six shawt,' and the third said, 'I have five shawt.' He (the Imam) said: 'If they all doubted, let them restart (perform Qada/Istinyaaf); and if they did not doubt and each one was certain of what he had, let them build upon it.'

key_terms.يَبْنُوا: Let them build upon (what is certain)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for Tawaf when worshippers have different counts of stages and doubt their completion?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Rida (AS) establishes the principle of 'building upon certainty' (al-bina' ala al-muqarrar) in ritual worship, distinguishing between collective doubt requiring a full restart and individual certainty allowing for continuity. It highlights the Shia juristic preference for preserving the validity of acts when possible, reflecting the broader legal maxim that doubt does not invalidate what was established by certainty.
